title: Mouse lncRNA knockouts resemble genes their papers name on other chromosomes nearly as much as named nearby genes, so phenotype resemblance in curated data is not evidence of local action
abstract:
In the curated mouse knockout record, the phenotype of a long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) knockout resembles the knockout phenotype of a gene that its paper names on another chromosome nearly as much as that of a named gene next to the lncRNA; enhancer and other regulatory-region knockouts show most of the same pattern. This matters because papers often argue that a non-coding knockout acts through its neighbouring gene when the two phenotypes are similar, and knockout phenotypes are the main whole-organism evidence that lncRNA loci have functions.

We used Mouse Genome Informatics (MGI) phenotype annotations (release of 2026-11-19). A resemblance score is the percentile of a target gene's knockout profile among 13,153 phenotyped protein-coding genes (0.5 = no resemblance); independent alleles of one gene score 0.762 and neighbouring protein-coding genes 0.510. Genes named in the titles or abstracts of lncRNA knockout papers score 0.841 (95% CI 0.758-0.913, 29 loci) when they lie within 1 Mb and 0.803 (0.739-0.860, 33 loci) when they lie on another chromosome. For regulatory-region knockouts the values are 0.904 and 0.780. Within loci that name both, near minus far is -0.015 (-0.20 to +0.14, 9 lncRNA loci) and +0.047 (-0.05 to +0.14, 19 regulatory loci); a modest position effect is therefore not excluded. lncRNA knockouts without a named nearby gene resemble their nearest gene slightly more than the protein-coding baseline (registered test +0.086, +0.010 to +0.163) and not clearly more than microRNA knockouts (+0.024, -0.083 to +0.131; +0.058 after removing microRNA host genes and Hox-cluster microRNAs).

In fission yeast, where lincRNA deletions were measured in the same conditions, the deletion profiles of 107 lincRNAs show no detectable resemblance to the deletion profiles of their neighbouring genes (0.474, 0.434-0.516; same gene in two screens 0.703), but this test has low sensitivity.

Limitations: 9 to 39 loci per comparison; curated data follow the authors' interests; the score ignores the direction of effects.

display.caption: Mouse knockouts: mean resemblance score (percentile of the target gene among 13,153 phenotyped protein-coding genes; 0.5 = no resemblance). Filled markers: a gene near the locus; open markers: genes the same papers name on other chromosomes. Near/far rows use exact mouse-symbol matching in titles and abstracts; the two "no gene named" rows use loci with no gene named within 1 Mb (symbol, upper case or synonym) scored against the nearest gene, without microRNA host genes and Hox-cluster microRNAs. Grey rows: same-gene ceiling and protein-coding neighbour baseline. Bars: 95% bootstrap intervals over loci.

Loci whose papers name both a gene within 1 Mb and genes on other chromosomes (exact symbol matching). Each line joins the score of the named nearby gene (filled) and the mean score of the named genes on other chromosomes (open) for one locus. The mean difference and its 95% bootstrap interval are in each panel title.

Fission yeast. (a) Mean percentile of the target gene's 2023 deletion-library profile among 3,451 genes, for 2022 deletion profiles over 37 matched conditions. The same coding gene scores 0.70; lincRNA deletions against their neighbouring genes score 0.47, near the coding-neighbour level. (b) Probability that a strain with no real effect gets at least one hit in 133 conditions, by per-test false-positive rate; blue line: share of lincRNA deletions with at least one published stress hit.
